content.title: Masters leaderboard, Round 3 updates, scores, Saturday highlights
content.text: Updated April 11, 2026, 7:25 p.m. ETMoving day at the 2026 Masters was a sight to behold. There were loads of birdies, bogeys, water balls and even a hole-in-one.Defending champion Rory McIlroy entered the day with a six-shot lead, the largest 36-hole advantage ever at the Masters, but he won't have any cushion going into the final round. After a 1-over 73 Saturday, McIlroy is in a tie for the with Cameron Young, who fired a blistering 65 to vault himself to the top of the leaderboard.Keep scrolling to see updates, scores, highlights and the best moments from Saturday's third round of the 90th Masters Tournament.2026 Masters leaderboardYou can see every score turned in at Augusta National with the 2026 Masters live leaderboard. Here's what it looked like at the top when play concluded Saturday:PositionPlayerScoreThruT1Cameron Young-11FT1Rory McIlroy-11F3Sam Burns-10F4Shane Lowry-9FT5Jason Day-8FT5Justin Rose-8FT7Scottie Scheffler-7FT7Haotong Li-7F Rory McIlroy shoots 73 Saturday at the MastersRory McIlroy made par at the 18th and finishes the third round of the Masters with a 1-over 73. It was a rollercoaster round for the defending champ, who made a double bogey, three bogeys and four birdies Saturday at Augusta. He's the only player in the top 10 who did not shoot par or better. Despite holding a six-shot advantage after 36 holes, he'll enter the final round in a tie for the lead with Cameron Young. Rory McIlroy bogeys No. 17, drops back into tie for leadRory McIlroy made par at No. 16 but bogeyed the 17th thanks to an errant tee shot that gave him loads of tree trouble on his approach. He drops back to 11 under and into a tie for the lead with Cameron Young, who's in the clubhouse with a 65. Rory McIlroy makes birdie at the 15th to take solo leadRory McIlroy regained the solo lead with his second of back-to-back birdies at the par-5 15th. He's one shot clear of Cameron Young with three holes to play as of 6:30 p.m. ET. Rory McIlroy birdies No. 14 to grab share of lead againRory McIlroy poured in a birdie putt at the 14th to rejoin a tie for the lead with Cameron Young, who is in the clubhouse at 11 under. Cameron Young fires 65 Saturday at the MastersCameron Young matched the low round of the tournament thus far with a 7-under 65 Saturday at the Masters. He was the solo leader at 11 under when he walked off the 18th green just after 6 p.m. ET. Sam Burns gets within one with birdie at the 13thSam Burns rolled in a long birdie putt at the 13th and has tied Rory McIlroy for second at 10 under, one shot off Cameron Young's lead. Shane Lowry birdies No. 14, joins tie for thirdShane Lowry birdied the 14th to get back to 9 under for the tournament and into a tie for third with Sam Burns as of 5:50 p.m. ET. Rory McIlroy bogeys No. 12, Cameron Young takes solo leadCameron Young is now the solo leader at the Masters after beginning Saturday's third round eight shots back. Rory McIlroy double-bogeyed No. 11 and bogeyed the 12th to drop back to 10 under. Young birdied No. 16 and sits alone at the top as of 5:40 p.m. ET. Cameron Young ties the lead with birdie at No. 16Rory McIlroy began the day with a six-shot lead. That lead is now gone. Cameron Young bounced back from his bogey at No. 15 with a birdie at the 16th to get to 11 under and join McIlroy at the top of the leaderboard as of 5:35 p.m. ET on Saturday. Rory McIlroy double-bogeys 11Moments after Cam Young rinsed his approach at the 15th, Rory McIlroy hooked his approach on No. 11 into the water. He took a drop and hit a brilliant pitch shot to about three feet, but missed the short bogey putt. His lead is now just one as he moves onto the 12th. Cameron Young finds the water on 15, saves bogeyCameron Young's momentum came to a screeching halt at the par-5 15th when his third shot found the water in front of the green. Fortunately for him, he threw a dart on his second approach after a drop and saved bogey to stay in solo second. Rory McIlroy birdies the 10th, takes two-shot leadRory McIlroy is in red numbers for the first time Saturday after a birdie at No. 10 got him to 1 under for the day and 13 under for the tournament. He's now two shots clear of Cameron Young, who's in solo second at 11 under as of 5:15 p.m. ET. Jason Day quietly moving up the leaderboardWith everyone's attention seemingly elsewhere, Jason Day has quietly creeped up the leaderboard. He made three birdies in a row on holes 12-14 to get to 8 under for the tournament and into a tie for third. Cameron Young gets within one Saturday at the MastersCameron Young is making Augusta National look easy Saturday. He made his second of back-to-back birdies at the 14th to get to 7 under for the day, 11 under overall and within one shot of Rory McIlroy's lead. Cameron Young moves into solo second with birdie at 13Cameron Young's tee shot at No. 13 smoked a tree and bounced back into the fairway. He took advantage of the break from the golf gods, making birdie on the par-5 to move into solo second on the leaderboard. Rory McIlroy shoots even-par 36 on the first nineRory McIlroy shot even-par 36 on the first nine of Saturday's third round at the Masters. He makes the turn with a two-shot lead ahead of Cameron Young. Shane Lowry bounces back with birdie at No. 10Shane Lowry nearly added another hole-out to his Augusta highlight reel with his approach shot at No. 10. He made birdie and got back to 9 under after a bogey at the ninth. Scottie Scheffler: 'I don't feel like I'm out of the tournament'Scottie Scheffler has two Masters titles, but he's never played as well in one round at Augusta as he did on Saturday. His 7-under 65 is the lowest round of Scheffler's Masters career in seven starts. Rory McIlroy staying steady Saturday at the MastersIt was a shaky start for Rory McIlroy with a bogey at No. 1, but he bounced back with a birdie at the third and remains even par through seven holes. Shane Lowry joins tie for secondShane Lowry, riding momentum from his ace at No. 6, birdied the eighth to get to 9 under for the tournament and into a tie for second with Haotong Li and Cam Young as of 4:30 p.m. ET. Scottie Scheffler fires 65, enters Sunday in contentionIf you thought Scottie Scheffler was just going to roll over and take his medicine this weekend, you thought wrong. The World No. 1 shot a bogey-free, 7-under 65 Saturday at the Masters and surged into the top 10 on the leaderboard. He'll enter Sunday firmly in contention, looking to secure his third green jacket. Cameron Young is on fire Saturday at the MastersCameron Young is absolutely "balling" as the kids say. He's 5 under through 10 holes Saturday at the Masters and has moved into a tie for second with Haotong Li as of 3:15 p.m. ET. Since start 4 over through the first 7 holes on Thursday, he's 13 under. Shane Lowry makes hole-in-one at Augusta's sixthDrinks are on Shane Lowry tonight! This beauty from the Irishman gets him to 8 under and within 4 shots of the lead. Read more about Lowry's long history of iconic aces. Scottie Scheffler birdies 16It's another birdie for Scottie Scheffler, who is working on the best round of the day. He's 7 under through 17 and has moved up to T-6 on the leaderboard. Collin Morikawa hoels out for eagle at 15Collin Morikawa's status entering this week was up in the air. He wasn't sure if he'd even play the Masters while he continues to recover from a back injury. Well, good thing he decided to give it a go, because not only did he make the cut, he's 3 under and in the top 20 thanks to this incredible shot at the par-5 15th on Saturday. Haotong Li moves to solo second at the MastersHaotong Li is not bothered by the loads of star power around him. He's cruising right along Saturday at Augusta, making three birdies and an eagle at the par-5 eighth to get to 9 under and into solo second. Patrick Reed bogeys, Rory McIlroy's lead back to 4Rory McIlroy is back on top by four shots after recovering from a slow start with a birdie at the third. Patrick Reed bogeyed the par-3 fourth to drop back to 8 under. Rory McIlroy gets back on track with birdie at No. 3Rory McIlroy drove the green and nearly holed his eagle putt at the par-4 third, but settles for birdie to get back to 12 under and take a three-shot lead. Patrick Reed pulls within twoWe've got a ballgame here, folks. Patrick Reed starts his third round with three straight birdies and has pulled within two shots of the lead after Rory McIlroy started bogey-par. Patrick Reed starts birdie-birdie, moves to solo secondPatrick Reed is off to a blistering start Saturday at the Masters, making birdies at Nos. 1 and 2 to get to 8 under and grab solo second as of 2:15 p.m. ET. Wyndham Clark makes rare eagle at the thirdWyndham Clark drove the green at the par-4 third and sunk the putt, marking just the 20th eagle ever at No. 3. He moves to 6 under, joining a crowded tie for fourth. Rory McIlroy bogeys No. 1, lead shrinks to fourAnd just like that, Rory McIlroy's lead has shrunk from six shots to four. McIlroy bogeyed No. 1 while Sam Burns and Patrick Reed each made birdie. Rory McIlroy begins his third round at the MastersRory McIlroy slept on the largest 36-hole lead in the history of the Masters. With big names already charging up the leaderboard, McIlroy has gotten his third round underway. Cameron Young holes out for birdie at No. 4Cameron Young makes birdie at the tough par-3 fourth to get to 6 under. Scottie Scheffler tied for second after another birdieScottie Scheffler began the day at even par and outside the top 20. After 11 holes, he's tied for second. The World No. 1 made his fourth birdie in five holes after throwing a dart at the 11th and rolling in an eight-foot putt. Scottie Scheffler makes 3 straight birdies, moves into top 5Just when you thought you could count him out... World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler rattled off three straight birdies to close out a bogey-free, 5-under 31 on the first nine Saturday at the Masters. As of 2:20 p.m. ET, the two-time Masters champ is tied for fourth. Rory McIlroy talks game plan for Saturday at AugustaRory McIlroy has the largest 36-hole lead in the history of the Masters, but he knows "there's a lot of golf left ahead of all of us, and a lot of things can happen on this golf course." Hideki Matsuyama makes 3-straight birdiesThe golfing pride of Japan is working his way up the leaderboard. Matsuyama made three straight birdies on holes 3-5 and has joined a tie for fourth as of 2:10 p.m. ET. Brian Harman fires 67 early Saturday at the MastersBrian Harman proved that there are low scores to be had Saturday at Augusta National. The lefty made six birdies to offset his lone bogey at the seventh and signed for a 5-under 67. Scottie Scheffler moves into top 10Don't look now, but Scottie Scheffler might be making a big move. The World No. 1 and two-time Masters champ is 4 under for the day after back-to-back birdies at Nos. 7 and 8. He joined a tie for ninth just after 2 p.m. ET. Chris Gotterup makes eagle to join tie for 4thChris Gotterup surged into the top 5 on the leaderboard early Saturday with an eagle at the par-5 second. A Masters rookie, Gotterup will be looking to make the most of his first moving day at Augusta, and he's off to a good start. Max Homa, Hideki Matsuyama start fast on moving dayMax Homa made back-to-back birdies to open his third round while 2021 Masters champ Hideki Matsuyama birdied two of his first four holes Saturday. Both players have moved into a tie for seventh at 4 under for the tournament. Rory McIlroy arrives at Augusta National for third roundRory McIlroy slept on a six-shot lead thanks to a pair of blistering rounds of 67 and 65 over the first two days at Augusta National. He could become just the fourth player to ever win back-to-back Masters titles. Will he maintain his lead entering Sunday? Or will someone charge up the leaderboard to put some pressure on him? Stay tuned to find out. Sepp Straka nearly dunks approach at No. 10Sepp Straka is working on the best round of the day thus far. He's 3 under and bogey-free through 10 holes, with his third birdie of the day coming as a result of this brilliant approach shot that nearly dropped in for an eagle. Aaron Rai pulls off insane shot from his kneesEveryone knows you have to get creative around Augusta National. This is about as creative as it gets from Aaron Rai, who won the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday. Scottie Scheffler starts hot Saturday at the MastersScottie Scheffler stuck his second shot at the par-5 second to six feet with a 7-wood, rolling in the putt for eagle to get to 2 under for the day and into a tie for 16th on the leaderboard. 2026 Masters prize money payouts revealedFamously, Augusta National Golf Club does not reveal the Masters prize money payouts until Saturday morning every year. That bulletin was just posted, and now we know how much money the winner of the 90th Masters stands to make. Click here to see the full purse breakdown. The Jordan Spieth Experience is off and running SaturdayThere's never a dull moment when Jordan Spieth is on the golf course, especially at Augusta National. Masters third round hole locationsHere's a look at the pin locations for Saturday's third round of the Masters: Masters Saturday weatherWe're in for another bright and sunny day at Augusta National Golf Club. It will be about 10 degrees warmer Saturday compared to the first two rounds, but still nearly perfect weather for golf.How to watch Masters SaturdayBelow is a look at the main broadcast schedule for Saturday's third round. For the full guide to streaming and alternate feeds, click here.Paramount+: 12-2 p.m. ETCBS/Paramount+: 2-7 p.m. ETMasters tee times for Saturday's third roundCheck out the third round tee times, with the first group off at 9:31 a.m. ET. Here's a look at Saturday's featured groups:Jon Rahm, Si Woo Kim (9:53 a.m. ET)Jordan Spieth, Sepp Straka (11:21 a.m. ET)Scottie Scheffler, Ludvig Aberg (12:16 p.m. ET)Brooks Koepka, Chris Gotterup (1:33 p.m. ET)Who's leading the 2026 Masters?That would be Rory McIlroy, who's at 12 under and leads by six. That's a Masters record for largest lead after 36 holes. Lurking is another past Masters champ: Patrick Reed.Which big names missed the cut at the Masters?There were several notable names who came up short of the low 50 and ties for the weekend.Jack Nicklaus had some blunt advice for Rory McIlroySix-time Masters champ had a discussion with the defending champion and told him quite specifically what he should avoid here in 2026.
